title: Preserve typed edit intent through durable operation results

requirements.invariant: A form owns only typed transient draft state and emits typed edit intent; it does not construct a provider patch, authorize a field, coordinate a multi-record write, infer server commitment, or import a backend SDK.

Submitting a validated draft binds stable Account, actor, contract, operation, subject, expected revision, and typed payload values through the shared operation envelope; queued, applied, rejected, conflicted, retryable, and required-update truth remains explicit.

Every edit submission carries the exact expected subject revision and refuses missing, duplicate-conflicting, wrong-subject, wrong-Account, or stale-operation binding rather than defaulting to last-write-wins.

Edit contracts contain only Ledger and standard Swift values; unchanged/set/clear is explicit, and arbitrary field names, dynamic dictionaries, null sentinels, document paths, SQL, SDK handles, and vendor errors cannot cross the boundary.
Deterministic provider-free fixtures prove draft restart, local receipt versus authoritative result, retry, rejection, conflict, required update, revision binding, and stale result refusal.

items: EditFieldValue<Value> is a closed generic value with unchanged, set(Value), and clear cases; set of an empty/zero value is not clear, and encoding preserves all three cases.

TypedEditDraft<Payload> binds a stable draft ID, AccountID, subject, expected UInt64 revision, optional local-data version, captured time, and a feature-owned typed payload conforming to TypedEditPayload; no raw field registry or dictionary exists.

EditDraftValidationIssue uses only a stable optional EditFieldID and EditValidationCode; EditDraftValidation returns unchanged, invalid with deterministic unique issues, or a non-publicly-constructible ValidatedEditDraft.

EditSubmissionBinding is created only from a validated draft and an OperationEnvelope whose Account matches and whose preconditions contain exactly one matching expectedRevision for the draft subject; it stores the canonical operation fingerprint.

EditSubmissionPresentation maps the shared OperationReceipt/OperationSnapshot into closed accepted/queued/applying/applied/rejected/conflicted/retryable/reauthenticate/requiredUpdate/superseded/resolved states after exact operation, Account, contract, and fingerprint validation.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: Shared form/draft/presentation values introduce no target relation, view, function, constraint, or index.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: This slice validates submission binding but executes no business command; feature handlers later revalidate product field policy and invariants.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Data API schema, relation, or function is exposed.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: No server row or function is introduced; authorization remains the feature handler and owning relation policy obligation.

syncStreams.notApplicable: This slice consumes shared operation results and local versions but defines no PowerSync Stream, subscription, or row visibility policy.

items: Typed drafts, field intent, validation issues, and queued operation envelopes encode deterministically and reconstruct without a network; the non-decodable submission binding is recreated only by revalidating that draft and envelope, and local validation does not claim server acceptance.
OperationReceipt means local durable acceptance only; authoritative presentation derives only from a matching OperationSnapshot and retains the shared queued/applying/applied/rejected semantics.

Wrong operation ID, Account, contract, fingerprint, draft subject revision, and stale/mismatched snapshots fail without replacing current edit-submission state; transient retry and conflict remain explicit.

storageMedia.notApplicable: No attachment identity, byte, object, URL, or durable capture behavior is introduced.

appMcp.notApplicable: Draft state is app presentation state. App and MCP later share the feature command payload/handler, while MCP does not consume UI drafts.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase form state, patch dictionary, NSNull sentinel, or transient view state is migrated.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: The shared value/presenter layer emits no telemetry; later feature slices may record stable operation/error categories without draft values.

items: The contracts are additive target-only Swift code, import no provider SDK, alter no current app project, contact no hosted service, and activate no production behavior.
Concrete feature drafts and editors opt in later; reverting this foundation before cutover removes only target-only code, tests, and transient target draft values.

verification.expected: Unchanged, set(empty/zero/nonempty), and clear remain distinct through application and encoding; typed payload change detection and stable field validation contain no raw patch mechanism.
Draft, validation, and accepted submission binding reconstruct identically from deterministic local bytes without implying server commitment or losing Account/subject/revision/fingerprint identity.
Missing/duplicate/wrong revision preconditions, wrong Account, changed payload fingerprint, wrong operation, and mismatched snapshots fail closed and do not mutate another draft's submission state.

Local receipt, retrying queue, applying, applied, validation rejection, conflict, authorization, reauthentication, required update, superseded, and resolved states map deterministically from the shared lifecycle without vendor errors.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: Immutable pull-request evidence containing the unchanged implementation passes conversion traceability, source-contamination and generated-contract checks, the complete target test suite, macOS and generic iOS Simulator target builds, and clean tracked-diff validation.

notes: Decision-independent technical-control foundation derived from the app-shell capability dossier. It stops before product field mutability/validation, money parsing or accounting, feature commands/handlers, concrete iOS/macOS forms, accessibility/visual evidence, Auth, local database/Sync/provider adapters, hosted resources, migration, release, or cutover authority.
